groups.reason: Catalog permissions, policy emission, execution dispatch and approval resolution agree on read escapes, contained writes and domain grants. Human and judge paths retain different stale-request checks; retries retain prior-result and grant-specific event order. ToolSessionState owns session grants and the work guard tracks actual asynchronous jobs.

Read/write confinement shares canonical path resolution while Git metadata is readable only. Edit batches and writes share ordered per-path locks and staleness checks; read/grep rendering has independent output budgets, glob/grep share traversal exclusions. Keep partial-edit failure semantics and host-config write differences.

Use queue membership as the sole running-state authority, reuse exit-status result construction for host and sandbox execution, and centralize shell-segment traversal for Git/Cargo classifiers. Keep lexer semantics, grant revalidation, per-session FIFO, cwd sharing, cancellation, capture/drain differences and denial attribution. Existing 72 sandbox-compatible bash tests pass.

Fetch independently checks URL/DNS/connected address and each redirect against session grants; search uses a fixed endpoint with bounded output and secret redaction. Generation-checked task registration prevents stale completion delivery. Transport/body formatting separation from the sixth sweep remains appropriate.

Task and MoA share terminal-event folding and a take-once termination registry. Task children survive a cancelled turn and retain reports; proposers are aborted with their pass. Keep requester-scoped lookup, notification provenance, partial-report handling and those distinct lifetimes.

Config writes retain TOML validation, read-before-write mtimes and atomic replacement; recall keeps query validation, database access and bounded display distinct. Memory updates use a finite field schema and explicit operations; knowledge dispatch remains a thin project-root adapter.

Separate the persisted knowledge document codec from project/store lookup and tool I/O. Preserve skill parsing differences, repository-root discovery order, fresh skill-body reads, role allowlists and trusted-project prompt/catalog gates. Existing 32 knowledge-related tests pass.

Keep trusted mediation context separate from tool arguments, two-stage parsing with escalation fallback, bounded asynchronous judgment and audit recording. Candidate identity is rechecked by approval resolution. Process-lifetime judge client configuration remains intentional existing behavior.

Shared RigAgentConfig defaults now initialize named providers, and registry construction has one provider creation path. Loader precedence, role overrides, picker two-stage selection, model-switch preservation, environment handoff and new-session-only reload remain unchanged.

Separated pre-generation retry classification and pacing from request/stream assembly. Reviewed both provider kinds, durable-output retry cutoff, cancellable backoff, stream timeouts, request-span closure and raw-vs-normalized tool arguments; existing retry and stream tests preserve ordering.

Reviewed queued/active input, stop handling, tool batches, truncation and memory recovery, MoA cancellation and guard halts. Fixed unused summary configuration by explicitly passing the tools-disabled config; loopback HTTP regression failed before and passed after, with original session config retained. Other event and cancellation ordering is preserved.

Centralized fallback event reconstruction while retaining authoritative-log precedence and untouched cross-session memory seeding. Clearing remains a request-only projection with occurrence counts, protected tail and current-round exclusions. Pairing repair keeps whole-history evidence separate from incremental repair; title summarizer retains its separate bounded request lifetime.

Mock scripts and their delayed cancellation path provide intentional deterministic protocol fixtures. Prior response extraction keeps startup/dispatch separate; their limited state machine is not merged with real provider recovery or tool execution.

Reviewed durable event contracts, live-only progress routing, incremental/replayed frame folding and caller queries. Centralized ProviderEvent defaults and reused pending-approval calculation on the post-TurnEnded slice; historical approval display remains unscoped. Kept turn status, tool occurrence identity and message promotion boundaries distinct.

Appender owns turn identity and session context; writer owns global sequence, ordered JSONL append and shared projection startup. Tolerant reads preserve the sequence high-water of undecodable events. Resume settles interrupted turns with restored TurnTracker before LiveState starts a new turn; current/rebuild/catch-up decisions remain together.

Reviewed transaction rollback, chunk bisection with malformed-record isolation, shared-store publication, event projection, bounded search/window queries and schema/record types. Domain-specific SQL bindings and projection shapes remain explicit; derived data remains rebuildable from JSONL. Benchmark helpers are retained as test-only callers.

Reviewed occurrence-aware tool/result folding, approval history, burst/turn boundaries, receipt aggregation and file effects against tool output producers. Combined grep/glob display construction with distinct labels. Retained separate error/superseded/unfinished paths and bounded text/diff formatting; no UI behavior change.

Reviewed provider startup, thread-local tool state, input/result dispatch, approval retries, recovery, environment activation, subscriptions and cleanup. Extracted durable input acceptance/delivery from approval dispatch and centralized record/flush/publish order, including end-of-runtime input failure. Startup recovery and explicit resume intentionally keep different validation/error policies; worktree ownership and grants remain validated before use.

Reviewed hello gating, per-attachment command/event channels, subscribe-before-replay, model/selection announcements, resume readiness and shutdown flush against shared wire types. Attachment lifetime is separate from session lifetime; transport limits remain explicit and provider reload applies through the existing connection seam.

Composer construction and updates share the same projection with an explicit dismissed approval. Plain-text rows delegate to the Markdown row renderer after escaping; grep/glob summaries share count formatting with their quote difference retained. Reviewed attachment generation, title refinement, notifications, task lifetime, turn/burst segmentation, stable-prefix scroller updates, receipts, approval actions and body limits. Keep separate cached transcript/status/composer entities, actionable versus historical approval queries and the broader in-flight state used by display clocks.

CLI option parsing and invoke decoding retain different caller defaults, confirmation and error contracts. Required strings and optional session UUIDs now have one decoder each; control requests use the existing runtime event-stream bridge. Reviewed command dispatch, explicit session actions, new-session inheritance, background lookup attachment and deferred model-switch replies.

Reviewed JSONL framing, version rejection, unknown-message handling, request identity, synchronous executor boundary and socket selection/bind lifecycle against the CLI client. Transport parsing and GPUI command validation have distinct responsibilities; retained the existing per-connection/thread model and error replies.

Layout insertion now delegates direct-leaf construction to split_pane. Reviewed command enablement, cursor/focus operations, close versus terminate, layout normalization and weight validation, spatial navigation, session metadata, inventory reconciliation and frozen snapshot types. Persistence validates before mutation and rejects cross-kind inventory conflicts; 145 workspace tests pass.

Host-tool and workspace-root channels use runtime event_stream, matching control-plane and session consumers. Four modal cancellations share focus restoration while confirmation keeps its distinct mode behavior. Reviewed command callers, reconcile and detached entities, runtime identity checks, two-phase restore, spawn inheritance, notifications, keymap reload, drag persistence and cached versus composite pane rendering. Keep separate terminal and agent reload/adoption policies and board arms untouched.

Palette, view chooser and session manager remain domain-specific List delegates with shared widget behavior. Filtering/selection/rendering is local; shell owns operations and modal lifetime. Session lineage uses cycle guards and preserves sibling order; subtree traversal deliberately returns ids rather than display rows. Launchable roles come from the role registry; command enablement comes from the command model. Small empty-state and selection boilerplate does not justify a new cross-domain UI layer.

Share PTY side-effect delivery between output and synchronized-update timeout paths, and CSI-u modifier/suffix encoding. Preserve input-priority drain budget, frame pacing, query replies, legacy key tables, OSC scanning, selection and color semantics. The strengthened timeout test requires a prior visible frame and verifies all side effects after timer flush; 132 terminal-core tests pass.

TerminalHost owns PTY creation, retry arbitration, command routing and subscriber replacement; shared daemon code owns listener/connection lifecycle and hub uses receive_pump. Subscription precedes creation, attach seed is installed under the subscriber lock, late duplicate spawns are killed, and frame-channel closure leaves Exited delivery active. Reviewed read/core/writer threads, cwd inheritance, resize forwarding and teardown; keep watch frames and discrete events separate and UI disconnect distinct from termination.

Share row background painting between live and history frames, including empty-text colored spans. Preserve row generation/epoch caching, viewport request anchoring, IME versus key deduplication, mouse modes and glyph geometry. Isolated GUI verifies markers, colors, hyperlinks and session/layout restoration; detailed geometry and paint orchestration remain intentionally explicit.

The host-tool channel pump now uses horizon_wire::receive_pump, matching both daemon hubs and preserving malformed-item logging and final-error termination. Reviewed runtime lifetime cancellation, per-domain routes, stale handle identity, synchronous reply bounds, pre-hello retry/recovery, establishment deadlines, explicit reload, session command bridges and attachment cleanup. Keep terminal post-hello liveness probing and watch-frame/event lanes separate from agent event streams; closing frames must still allow terminal Exited delivery.

Shared crate owns wire ids/version negotiation, HelloGate, item-size limits, decode skip logging and server connection cleanup. Runtime clients add their own bounded establishment and recovery policy; test clients and low-level connect helpers retain distinct failure contracts. Reviewed daemon socket/env/binary resolution, listener/run/serve lifecycle, protocol schema recursion and command-line checker. Existing additive rules intentionally distinguish appended enum variants, optional properties, required constraints and version markers.

Binary lookup/link retry, isolated persistence paths, hub connection and process cleanup already have separate owners. AgentdSpawn persists the same options for restart tests; respawn/kill-and-keep-paths deliberately preserve data while Drop removes only owned artifacts. Test helper panics and bounded retries differ from production recovery. Compared shared users in daemon e2e/runtime tests and production connection helpers.

Host owns the WASM plugin, shared theme source and root; reload drops pending load/names tasks before replacing them. ArtifactWatch owns watcher and debounce task; retarget replaces watches only for changed paths. Guest theme/window projection, surface key forwarding, schema and sample remain separate; board registry entries are excluded. Native callers and WASM gate confirm the shared boundary.

Reuse one contrast normalization rule for derivation, editor initialization and slider values. Save through fallible TableLike access instead of assuming external TOML has normal tables; regression tests reproduce both scalar and valid inline-table panics, then cover unchanged invalid files and preserved inline values. Keep ordered seed derivation, color space math, presentation projections and live/saved ownership separate.

Share filesystem grant identity, type and breadth checks between retained session grants and freshly applied capabilities. Preserve the retained-grant absolute-path precheck and capability-build error behavior, revalidation after canonicalization, excluded subpaths and per-spawn validation. Config normalization, helper discovery, TMPDIR, Linux supervision and macOS denial attribution remain distinct. macOS paths were reviewed in source, not executed on this Linux host.

Open and network mediation have distinct syscall data, notification validation and enforcement paths. Keep excluded-path precedence, read-probe handling, rate limits and deny recording, trusted endpoint fd duplication, native BPF assembly, single-threaded fork/subreaper lifecycle and credential-checked bounded reports. Initial-capability selection remains explicit; callers preserve report ownership and process-tree cleanup.

Exact normalized host matching is the shared authority for CONNECT and HTTP; CONNECT remains opaque without TLS interception. Session proxy owns listener/task lifetime and a shared allowlist; per-command denial drain is serialized by the existing bash FIFO. Keep transport/denial evidence separate from tool-level redirect and public-address checks.

Entry separates CLI routing from native GUI startup and WASM exports. Shared runtime panic capture preserves thread-local locations and prior hooks; daemon and provider callers retain phase-specific recovery. Desktop notifications escape markup and route by session UUID; terminal and agent reuse title normalization. Input tracing stays opt-in. Board module declarations are outside the audit.
